transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... work has just become a real issue for me lately. We got a new operations manager, and ever since he started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I just can’t seem to leave work at work. 

I come home completely wound up. I end up snapping at my husband, and I lie awake at night just replaying meetings in my head. And then the next day, I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. It's just really getting to me, and I need to figure out how to handle it.
Do you find that you feel this same level of persistent worry and tension about other areas of your life outside of your work situation, such as your finances, your health, or your family's safety?

No, not really. It's honestly just work. My husband and I are doing fine financially, and everyone's healthy. I don't find myself worrying about our safety or paying the bills or anything like that. It all just comes back to the plant and this new manager. That's the only thing making me feel this tense.
Beyond the tension and worry you've described, have you been feeling particularly sad, hopeless, or less interested in the things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or anything like that. I still enjoy my weekends when I can actually get my mind off the plant for a minute. I mean, I'm frustrated and stressed out, sure, but I don't feel sad... just really aggravated about how things are going at my job.

When you are feeling this way at work or at home, do you find that you are acting out, such as being reckless, behaving in ways that are out of character, or perhaps neglecting your usual responsibilities?

I wouldn't say I'm being reckless, but... I am definitely slipping on my responsibilities. My work record has taken a bit of a hit lately. I've missed a few internal deadlines, which isn't like me, and I've been pulling back from meetings I'm expected to be at, just to avoid dealing with the new manager. 

And at home... well, like I said, I've been snapping at my husband, so we're arguing a lot more than usual. I'm also just not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to. I'm just too drained and wound up by the time I get home.

When you mentioned pulling back from meetings and missing deadlines, would you say your main problem is that you are intentionally avoiding these tasks, or is it more that you are physically or mentally unable to complete them due to your stress?

I think... well, it's mostly that I'm just trying to avoid him. I mean, physically, I can still do the work. I know how to do my job. But mentally, I just get so tense even thinking about interacting with this new manager that I'd rather just skip the meeting altogether. So, yeah, I guess I am intentionally staying away from those situations. 

As for the deadlines, that's probably more just me being so distracted and stressed out by all of this that I can't focus on the tasks like I usually do. It's not that I'm incapable of doing the work, my brain is just too wrapped up in the frustration of it all.
When you say you are snapping at your husband and pulling back from your responsibilities, would you say your behavior has become defiant, rebellious, or destructive toward others or property?

No, definitely not. I'm not breaking things or trying to be rebellious. I'm 55 years old, I'm not a teenager acting out. I'm just irritable. When I snap at my husband, it's just me being short-tempered because I'm so stressed from work, not because I'm trying to be mean or destructive. And I'm certainly not damaging any property or anything like that.
When you are feeling this way, do you find that you are also experiencing any physical symptoms of depression, such as significant changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My appetite is pretty much the same as it always is. I'm eating normally. And my sleep... well, I'm still sleeping okay. I might feel a lot more drained at the end of the day from all the stress, but my actual sleep schedule hasn't really changed. So, no, neither of those have been an issue for me.
When you are at home or at work, do you find yourself feeling a sense of emptiness or a loss of pleasure in your daily activities, even if you wouldn't describe it as full-blown sadness?

No, I wouldn't say I feel empty. I still enjoy the things I usually do when I'm at home. I mean, once I can finally get my mind off work, I still like my normal routines and I still enjoy my weekends. It's really just the frustration with my manager that's bothering me so much. But overall, no, I haven't lost interest in my life or anything like that.
When you are feeling this way at work, do you find that you experience physical sensations like a racing heart, trembling, or feeling like you are on the verge of a panic attack?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. My heart isn't racing or pounding, and I'm not shaking or anything. I definitely don't feel like I'm having a panic attack. It's more just... a constant, heavy stress, you know? I get irritable and frustrated, but I don't get those intense physical feelings like you're describing.
When you are feeling this way, do you find yourself feeling more anxious and worried about the situation, or do you find yourself feeling more down, tearful, or hopeless about it?

I don't really think it's either of those. I'm not... I'm not sitting around crying or feeling hopeless about everything. And I wouldn't say I'm anxious or worried, either. It's really just that constant stress and frustration with my manager that I mentioned before. I'm just fed up with how things are going there, but I don't feel down or panicked about it.
Even though you don't feel hopeless, do you find that you have been experiencing periods of feeling sad, tearful, or down in the dumps since this situation at work began?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't been crying or... or feeling sad like that. It's really just what I said before—just being completely fed up and stressed out by my manager. I wouldn't say I feel down in the dumps at all.
